Subject: Weekly inventory safety margin & reserved capacity gating

Team —

Following up on this morning's growth call: we need a single, agreed safety margin to hold against Q3 reserved capacity requests so sales can surface realistic lead times to customers. Current ask from Acme (cc'd) would consume ~220 dedicated A100-equivalent cards over a 12-month commit window. Before we commit, we need: 

- A quick sanity check from infra (Karthik/Vivek) on runrate impact if we add 220 units starting Aug 1. Call out any hot months where capacity tightness interacts with existing rollouts.
- Finance (Laura/Aditya) to confirm cashflow/legal gating — if we approve a 12-month reserved slab with standard milestone-based billing, what shape of payment terms would you need to sign off?
- Marcus/SoJin: ops/console impacts — what SLO/monitoring changes do we need to enable for a large reserved pool (labeling, quotas, throttles)?

Attached: Q2_pipeline_snapshot.xlsx (filtered deck), reserved_capacity_safety_model_v3.csv (simple Monte Carlo sim), sizing_playbook.pdf (runbook checklist).

Request: please reply with bullet answers by EOD so I can share a combined note with sales and Acme. If anyone needs a quick sync, propose a 20m slot — I can do 11:30-12:00 or 15:00-15:30 PT.

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan —

Quick infra read: 220 A100-eq starting Aug 1 is feasible but not without shifting a couple of planned maintenance windows (notably a kernel/driver refresh in early Sep). If we provision naively, peak-week token throughput risk increases ~18% vs forecast and we'd see a 12-18% bump in node saturation across us-west deployments in the months after provisioning.

Options to mitigate:
- Stagger activation across two weeks (recommended) to flatten startup bump.
- Offer Acme a canary tranche (50 units) with immediate provisioning, hold the remainder on a 30-day activation notice.
- If finance requires a hard start date, we can reserve cold inventory (uninitialized GPUs) but that increases cost by ~4% (capex vs run).

I ran the attached safety_model against our rolling forecast. With a 15% safety margin, we stay comfortable through Q3 with current committed deals. If we drop to <10% we risk high contention weeks that will affect latency SLOs. Happy to present the sim tomorrow morning.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infra Capacity, Redwood Inference

Jordan —

From a finance perspective: a 12-month commit with milestone billing aligned to deployment makes sense. Two requests: 

1) We need a clear cancellation/falloff clause tied to utilization thresholds (e.g., if utilization < 50% for >60 days we step down the reserved slab). Sales should own the utilization reporting cadence.
2) Payment terms: standard is 45 days net for enterprise, but for large reserved capacity I'd prefer 30 days net with a 10% prepayment to cover initial setup. If Acme pushes back, we can trade a shorter billing cadence for a small premium in unit pricing.

If we accept the staggered activation (Karthik's suggestion), we should reflect that in the SOW and in the billing milestones. Happy to draft the billing paragraph and the falloff language — will send a redline by EOD.

Laura
Laura Bennett

Ops note: adding 220 units will require two small changes to the console and routing rules: 

- Add a reserved pool label (customer:acme, reserved:true) and enforce quota ceilings per-project. This is straightforward — ETA 5 dev-days (I can spin up a small sprint).
- Add a traffic-shaping policy so reserved requests degrade gracefully to on-demand model variants if the reserved pool is saturated. That will take 2 additional dev-days and a short runbook update.

We should also add a monitoring dashboard widget showing reserved pool utilization and a weekly digest that goes to Sales and Finance. If we include the staggered activation plan, we can smooth the initial alert noise.
